ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $O$ is the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$, and $AD$ is the diameter of $O$ with $CD$ connected. If $AD=3$ and $AC=2$, what is the value of $\cos B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AD$ is the diameter of circle $O$,\\
it follows that $\angle ACD=90^\circ$,\\
and therefore $DC=\sqrt{AD^{2}-CD^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}-2^{2}}=\sqrt{5}$,\\
Given that arc $AC$ equals arc $AC$,\\
it implies that $\angle B = \angle D$,\\
thus $\cos B = \cos D = \frac{DC}{AD} = \frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$.\\
Hence, $\cos B = \boxed{\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}}$.
